| `kube-bench` | `4.1.1` | `cluster` | NIS2 Art.21(2)(i), DORA Art.9, ISO27001:2022 A.8.2 |  | guidance only | No code is generated: removing a binding can lock out people or break controllers. List the cluster-admin bindings: kubectl get clusterrolebindings -o json \| jq -r '.items\[\] \| select(.roleRef.name=="cluster-admin") \| .metadata.name + ": " + (\[.subjects\[\]? \| .kind + "/" + .name\] \| join(", "))'. Keep the system: bindings of the provider. For each other subject, bind a narrower role, then remove the old binding: kubectl delete clusterrolebinding NAME. On EKS also check access entries with AmazonEKSClusterAdminPolicy (aws eks list-access-entries --cluster-name CLUSTER). |
| `kube-bench` | `4.1.3` | `cluster` | NIS2 Art.21(2)(i), DORA Art.9, ISO27001:2022 A.5.15, ISO27001:2022 A.5.18 |  | guidance only | List the roles with \* in apiGroups, resources or verbs: kubectl get roles,clusterroles -A -o json \| jq -r '.items\[\] \| select(any(.rules\[\]?; ((.apiGroups // \[\]) + (.resources // \[\]) + (.verbs // \[\])) \| index("\*"))) \| .kind + " " + (.metadata.namespace // "-") + " " + .metadata.name'. Leave cluster-admin and the built-in system: roles. In your own roles, replace \* with the API groups, resources and verbs the subjects use, then re-scan. |
| `kube-bench` | `4.1.4` | `cluster` | NIS2 Art.21(2)(i), DORA Art.9, ISO27001:2022 A.5.15 |  | guidance only | Give each workload that calls the Kubernetes API its own service account. Then stop the token of the default service account in each namespace: kubectl patch serviceaccount default -n NAMESPACE -p '{"automountServiceAccountToken": false}'. Remove RoleBindings and ClusterRoleBindings that grant rights to a default service account. Caution: Pods that still use the default service account lose API access when they restart. |
| `kube-bench` | `4.1.5` | `cluster` | NIS2 Art.21(2)(i), DORA Art.9, ISO27001:2022 A.5.15 |  | guidance only | List the pods that do not turn the token off in the pod spec: kubectl get pods -A -o json \| jq -r '.items\[\] \| select(.spec.automountServiceAccountToken \!= false) \| .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'. For workloads that do not call the Kubernetes API, set automountServiceAccountToken: false in the pod template or in their service account. Caution: A pod that calls the API without a token fails after its next restart. |

| `kube-bench` | `4.2.1` | `cluster` | NIS2 Art.21(2)(i), NIS2 Art.21(2)(g), DORA Art.9, ISO27001:2022 A.8.9 |  | guidance only | kube-bench reports this control as manual (WARN). List the pods that would break first: kubectl label --dry-run=server --overwrite ns --all pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=baseline. Fix or move them, then label each namespace with user workloads: kubectl label --overwrite ns NAMESPACE pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=baseline. Labels in warn or audit mode (pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn=baseline) report without blocking. |
